messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I see a throughput drop on reg-rl workload when ~70-90% of requests are prefix-cache hits. GPU util drops and p99 token latency jumps.
sam: Seen evidence of that in staging traces too. Any profiling snapshots?
maria: Pasted the critical bits below from the trace (staging canary):
```
workload: reg-rl-2026-03
pattern: 80% prefix hits, short completion length (15-40 tokens)
avg batch size (requests): 4.2
avg effective tokens/batch: 48
GPU util (device): 22%
serving p95 token latency: 48ms
p99 token latency: 210ms
kernel chosen: small-matrix path (fast small batch kernel) 85%
```
Observation: because prefix hits collapse the runtime's measured sequence length we frequently fall into the 'small kernel' branch which has high per-token overhead for our payload shape, and the dynamic batcher is forming many tiny microbatches.
kai: That matches what i saw — cache hits reducing "observed length" causes the continuous-batcher to lower token budget and then the kernel switch kills throughput. Could tried to treat cache-hit tokens as "virtual length" so they contribute to batch formation without triggering KV recompute.
ashley: Can we adjust queue policy instead (e.g., increase window ms or min_tokens) rather than changing kernel thresholds? Might be lower risk.
maria: Agreed on conservative approach. Proposed experiments: 1) occupancy-window smoothing: keep a rolling occupancy that counts cache-hit tokens as 0.5 effective tokens for batch formation; 2) raise min_batch_tokens to 128; 3) change wait_for_batch_ms from 6 -> 15 for high-hit ratio flows; 4) add a kernel-selector fallback that uses throughput profile instead of raw seq_len at < 50 tokens.
sam: Nice. Quick config sketch for batcher canary: \n```yaml\nbatcher:\n  mode: continuous\n  occupancy_window_ms: 40\n  cache_hit_virtual_weight: 0.5\n  min_batch_tokens: 128\n  target_batch_tokens: 512\n  max_wait_ms: 15\nkernel_selector:\n  small_kernel_threshold_tokens: 32 # keep, but prefer throughput fallback if util < 40%\n  prefer_throughput_if_util_below: 0.4\n```\nThis will let cache-hits contribute but still preserve the safety net.
kai: Also add a metric: batch_effective_token_rate = total_tokens_sent_to_kernel / batch_formation_time. We need to alert if that drops by >20% post-change.
ashley: Be careful with latency SLO — increasing wait window can bump p95. Suggest we do an A/B where 10% of traffic uses new batcher config and we measure token/sec, p95 tokens, and cost-per-token.
maria: Plan: implement config flags behind runtime feature flag `prefill_virtualize_v1`, deploy to canary 10% on reg-rl, collect 6h rolling metrics. If GPU util increases and p99 drops we roll to 50%. If p95 increases >10% and p99 not decreasing, rollback.
perf-bot: deploy canary started: canary-id=pfv1-2103, routes: reg-rl-*, duration=6h
sam: Also log kernel selection reasons in traces (small_kernel vs large_kernel) with a tag `ks.reason` so we can compute selection frequency pre/post.
kai: One more thought: kernel microbenchmarks show the small-matrix kernel has higher per-token launch overhead for sequences >40 due to extra head-copy on some hw. We should schedule a follow-up to profile kernel paths with synthetic prefix-hit shapes.
maria: Assigned tasks: sam -> implement feature flag + config; kai -> add metrics + microbench harness; ashley -> set up A/B dashboards and alerts; i'll run the canary and synth tests. Target: start canary in next 2 hours.
ashley: ack :thumbsup:
sam: PR up in 10m, will post link when ready.
maria: thanks all, i'll post canary link and initial grafana panels once traffic ramps up. :rocket:
